lede: Marshall carries a full EdgeDesk team rating at -4.9; Gardner-Webb is not one of the 138 FBS programmes EdgeDesk rates, so the comparison is one-sided by construction rather than by judgement.
EdgeDesk makes it Marshall -24.8 before any sportsbook number is consulted, with Marshall winning 95% of simulations.

The roster and position-group comparison below explains where EdgeDesk’s separation comes from on the side it can measure; Gardner-Webb is absent from the FBS player dataset, so the exact size of that gap is not established.
Data confidence on this matchup is 43% — enough to publish, not enough to treat the exact margin as settled.

favourite.heading: Why Marshall can pull away
bullets: Marshall is the better football team by 21.0 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 64% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+21.0 pts).
Playing at Marshall is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Gardner-Webb can keep it close
bullets: Stylistically the matchup favours Gardner-Webb by 0.3 points: early-down offence vs early-down defence (-0.3 pts).
The outcome range is 15.1 points wide at one sigma — p10 +1.8 to p90 +45.8 for Marshall, so a projection of +24.8 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 3%.
50% of the model’s own input contract was empty for this game — no starter, injury or per-player talent context reached it, so the number leans on team strength more than it should.
Gardner-Webb is not in the FBS rating set, so EdgeDesk cannot measure what it does well. An unmeasured opponent is an unknown, not a weak one, and the size of the gap is not established.
